outcomes.target: The woman is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head.
outcomes.reference: The woman in the input image.

nodes.question: Does the image show a helmet visibly on the woman’s head?
nodes.criteria: Pass if a helmet is visibly on the woman’s head; fail if the image clearly shows no helmet on her head; unknown if the woman or her head is not visible enough to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess only the woman in the input image and whether she is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head. Ignore unrelated edits.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show the source woman with a helmet-related change that is visibly incomplete—for example, a helmet being placed but not yet on her head?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if visible evidence shows a helmet-related change to the source woman that is in progress and not yet complete. Fail if no helmet-related change is visible, or if the helmet is already visibly on her head as a complete result. Unknown if the woman, helmet, or placement cannot be judged.
nodes.binding: Compare the edited image with the source, identify the same woman, and assess only visible helmet placement on her head. A helmet merely nearby, on another subject, or already present in the source is not progress. Do not infer incompleteness from uncertainty.

nodes.question: Is a helmet visibly present on the woman’s head?
nodes.criteria: For R1, complete if s1 passes. Partial only if s1 fails and s2 passes, establishing both no completed helmet-on-head result and visible incomplete helmet-related progress. Absent if s1 and s2 both fail. Unknown if these states do not establish complete, partial, or absent; in particular, s1 unknown with s2 pass remains unknown. Unrelated edits do not count as progress; insufficient evidence remains unresolved.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is already appropriately focused on whether the helmet is visibly on the woman’s head; the edited image clearly shows this, and the two valid s1 observations support completion. Do not alter the visual criterion to chase the unresolved cases: those are explicitly transport failures, not negative image evidence. The node’s unknown outcomes arise because its required s1/s2 dependencies are unavailable, while other runs complete despite s2’s contradictory, high-confidence rationale (it calls a fully worn helmet “in progress” while marking fail). Preserve the complete/partial/absent distinctions, but make the typed criteria and dependency routing unambiguous: a passing s1 establishes complete fulfillment; s2 is relevant to partial progress only when s1 fails, and must not veto a pass. Treat call/transport failures as unresolved evidence rather than visual fail, and avoid letting repeated high-confidence but internally contradictory s2 judgments override direct completion evidence. This should improve coverage without weakening the requested check or treating the reference label as atomic ground truth.
s2: The binding is misaligned with the actual instruction: it asks whether a helmet is being placed but not yet on her head, whereas the request is simply to give the woman a helmet. The edited image visibly shows the source woman wearing a helmet, so this is complete fulfillment, not partial progress. Keep s2 narrowly about genuine incomplete helmet progress, but ensure it is routed only when the completion check s1 fails; a passing s1 must establish completion and must not be vetoed by s2. Make the typed criteria and routing explicit so “helmet already on her head” is not treated as evidence for partial progress. Preserve unknown for insufficient visual evidence, and keep transport/call failures unresolved rather than interpreting them as visual negatives. The repeated high-confidence fail traces are internally consistent with s2’s incomplete-progress criterion, but they do not contradict completion; the issue is criterion/routing ambiguity, not a reason to weaken the requested check. The transport failure is separate and should not drive a semantic edit.
s1: The binding is already well aligned with the requested edit: the edited image visibly shows a helmet worn on the woman’s head, and valid s1 traces agree. Do not change the visual criterion to explain unresolved runs: those are explicit transport failures, not negative image evidence. For typed structural edits, clarify routing so a valid s1 pass establishes completion and any partial-progress check is consulted only after s1 fails; it must not veto a pass. Keep transport failures unresolved, and preserve unknown for genuinely insufficient visual evidence. The low aggregate coverage therefore calls for fixing failure handling/routing, not weakening or replacing the helmet-on-head check.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment readout cannot faithfully distinguish a complete result from partial progress. s2 is defined to pass only when it shows progress but does not establish the complete result in s1, yet the readout says partial if s1 does not pass and s2 passes. If s1 is unknown while s2 passes, this can label the result partial without establishing incompleteness; if s1 fails, the checks may also conflict about whether a helmet is present. The composition should require evidenced incompleteness before assigning partial and resolve contradictory support observations rather than treating them as a valid outcome.

The support checks do not provide sufficient evidence to distinguish partial progress from a complete result. s2 asks whether a helmet is on or being placed on the woman’s head, but its pass criterion also requires that the evidence not establish the complete result in s1. That completeness judgment is not an independent visual proposition for the support check to assess, and the fulfillment readout cannot reliably derive it from the saved observations. Consequently, the program can leave genuine partial progress unresolved or misclassify it; the readout’s conflict rule does not repair this gap.

The fulfillment rule is incomplete for the rubric’s unresolved-evidence case. If s1 is unknown but s2 passes, it returns unknown even though the visible addition evidence establishes progress and the helmet’s completion status remains unresolved; the rubric calls for partial when some progress is evidenced without complete fulfillment. The rule also makes partial conditional on s1 failing, so it cannot faithfully compose that known progress with an unknown completion observation.
